adaptation_proposal.listing_description: Application-level Amazon Cognito authentication and client-session guidance covering user-pool flows, OAuth/OIDC, token selection, refresh-token rotation, revocation, safe storage, and authorizer integration.
use_when: A browser or mobile client needs Cognito sign-in, OAuth/OIDC, or token lifecycle guidance.
A configured Cognito app client is being migrated to refresh-token rotation or revocation.
A team needs to choose the correct token and refresh operation for an existing Cognito user pool client.
do_not_use_when: The task is Amplify Gen2 backend definition work.
The task is IAM, STS, IAM Identity Center, or trust-policy authoring.
The task is API Gateway route/integration or Lambda implementation beyond Cognito authorizer behavior.

two_file_manifest_intent.SKILL.md: Use as the top-level selector and safety boundary: distinguish user pools from identity pools, identify public versus confidential clients, and enforce full-replacement read-modify-write for client updates.
two_file_manifest_intent.references/tokens-and-sessions.md: Use for the detailed token lifecycle procedure: rotation compatibility, retry grace, replacement-token persistence, supported refresh APIs, revocation reach, and storage/session nuances.

source_grounded_procedure.procedure: Read the current app-client configuration before changing it because the client update operation is a full replacement; preserve and resend every existing field.
Enable refresh-token rotation with the chosen retry grace period while retaining the existing OAuth, token-validity, scope, and flow settings that remain compatible.
Remove ALLOW_REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH from explicit authentication flows when rotation is enabled; the legacy REFRESH_TOKEN_AUTH path is rejected at runtime under rotation.
Refresh through GetTokensFromRefreshToken or the OAuth token endpoint with grant_type=refresh_token, then atomically store and use the newest refresh token returned by each successful refresh.
source_grounded_procedure.locator: Refresh token rotation, lines 67-74 and Common Errors, lines 193-199
